source.name: U.S. Census Bureau, 2022 Census of Governments: Finance (Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances)
source.table: Table 1. State and Local Government Finances by Level of Government and by State: 2022

lines.revenue: Line 1 Revenue (total: general, utility, liquor store and insurance trust revenue)
lines.fromFederal: Line 4 Intergovernmental revenue from Federal Government
lines.spending: Line 54 Expenditure (total, incl. utility, liquor store and insurance trust expenditure)
lines.debt: Line 125 Debt outstanding (end of fiscal year)

notes: Main figures are state and local governments combined; duplicative transactions between the state and its local governments are excluded, as the Census does. 'stateOnly' is the state government alone, as the same table gives it. Its 'spending' includes aid the state pays to local governments (intergovernmental expenditure), so state-only and combined figures cannot simply be subtracted or added. Its by-function figures are only the state's own direct spending: state aid passed to school districts, for example, is not in stateOnly.elementarySecondary.

'spending' is total expenditure (Census line 54), which includes utility, liquor store and insurance trust (e.g. pension and unemployment benefit) spending; 'directGeneralSpending' (line 66) leaves those out and is the base for the by-function figures.
By-function figures are direct expenditure. Education includes higher education, elementary & secondary and other education. Hospitals and health are separate Census lines.
Fiscal years differ by state (most end June 30); 'FY2022' means each government's fiscal year ending within July 2021 - June 2022.
Census: 'The data in this table come from a census of state and local governments and are not subject to sampling error.' Nonsampling error and nonresponse can still affect figures.

Newer years (FY2023, FY2024) are published by the Census only through data.census.gov / the Census API and raw public-use files, not as this ready-made table; FY2022 is the latest year with the published by-state summary table.
